newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares firm at open, sentiment upbeat.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares firm at open, sentiment upbeat.

text.p: Singapore shares opened firmer on Friday with blue chips continuing their rally from Thursday.
"The market is very strong. I think it will continue to be good in the morning but some profit-taking is expected later as the weekend is coming," said a dealer with a local firm.

She said the strong close on Wall Street overnight also aided sentiment. Funds continue to focus on heavyweights like DBS foreign, OCBC foreign and Sembawang Corp which all continued to climb in active dealing.
After about 25 minutes of trading, the key Straits Times Industrials Index was up 11.10 points to 2,200.86.
Volume was 35 million units with 193 gainers and 18 losers.
Newly listed luxury goods retailer FJ Benjamin topped the actives but eased four cents (US2.8 cents) to Singapore $1.15. Dealers say fair value for the stock is between S$1.10-S$1.20.
Kim Eng Warrants '97 also saw brisk trade and was up 2 cents to 31 cents. A dealer said there was speculative interest as the warrant was due to expire in February.
Hotel Properties was also active on talk that a covered warrant was being issued for the counter, said one broker.
Top gainers were Jurong Shipyard, Singapore Press foreign and DBS while Keppel Corp and Wing Tai fell.
